finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts::read-only notes mounts are enforced only at the view layer (`editorview.editable`), which the new undo gating treats as a write-permission check; keymap-driven commands can still dispatch changes that `notesync` pushes into the crdt for a viewer-role share link.
evidence: editor.ts sets only `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` and never `EditorState.readOnly`; per CodeMirror's documented semantics, `editable: false` removes contenteditable but does not stop keymap-driven or programmatic dispatch. `keymapExt()` binds `indentWithTab` unconditionally (no readOnly branch), and `indentMore` bails only on `state.readOnly`, so a Tab-driven `input.indent` transaction would flow through `note-sync.ts` update() (which matches 'input') into `YorkieNoteStore.editText`'s `doc.update` — and the server backstop in yorkie-auth.controller.ts defaults to shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` returns allow). The new `route()`/historyKeymap comments do treat `EditorView.editable` as a write-permission test, as claimed. I mark severity minor rather than higher because shared viewers are forced into `viewMode="view"`, which hides the editor pane (`display: none`), making the path hard to reach without devtools, and the `editable`-only pattern predates this diff; I could not read @codemirror/commands or verify contentDOM focusability in a read-only mount, hence medium confidence.
